# @unone/ui

Official pure Luau UI constructors, versioned with the portable Unone SDK.
The package returns ordinary existing UI nodes and uses the official player.
It supplies no colors, fonts, responsive rules, automatic layout or game state.
The [full component guide](../../docs/ui-components.md), style contract and
canonical strict types accompany the portable SDK's verified package inventory.

Declare the exact installed version in `project.unone.json`:

```json
{"runtime_packages":{"@unone/ui":"0.2.0"}}
```

The SDK includes the manifest and source at `packages/unone-ui/`. The matching
runtime exposes `api.ui.components`; no `require`, network download or additional
renderer is involved. `api.ui.components.info()` reports the installed metadata
and whether the current project declared it. Other methods fail with
`UI_PACKAGE_NOT_DECLARED` until the project declares that exact version.

```luau
local ui = api.ui.components.create({
    text={font_size=2,color={0.9,0.95,1,1}},
    button={font_size=2,padding={left=1,right=1}},
})
local cardId = "settings"
local card = ui.component({
    id=cardId, component="app.settings_card",
    rect={x=10,y=10,width=80,height=60},
    surface={kind="panel",style={background={0.03,0.05,0.08,1}}},
    children={
        ui.text({id=ui.id(cardId,"heading"),text="Settings",
            rect={x=15,y=55,width=70,height=8}}),
        ui.button({id=ui.id(cardId,"apply"),text="Apply",action="ApplySettings",
            rect={x=60,y=15,width=25,height=8}}),
    },
})
api.ui.setRoot(ui.screen({id="settings_screen",node="settings",children={card}}))
```

All constructors are available on both `api.ui.components` (without a theme) and
the kit returned by `create(theme?)`. The direct entry points call the same
implementation; they are not documentation-only aliases.

| Entry | Existing contract returned |
| --- | --- |
| `text(props)` | `UiTextNode` |
| `button(props)` | `UiButtonNode` |
| `slider(props)` | `UiSliderNode` |
| `combobox(props)` | `UiComboBoxNode` |
| `panel(props)` | `UiPanelNode` |
| `image(props)` | `UiImageNode` |
| `component(props)` | `UiComponentNode`, with optional surface |
| `screen(props)` | `UiScreen`, for `api.ui.setRoot` |
| `scrollView(options)` | Existing scroll helper's `UiScrollNode` |
| `virtualList(options)` | Existing list helper's live `UiScrollNode` |
| `virtualGrid(options)` | Existing grid helper's live `UiScrollNode` |

The same entries also include `id` and `composeStyle`. Theme fields are exactly
`text`, `button`, `slider`, `combobox`, `panel`, `image`, each an optional
`UiStyle`. No defaults apply to screens, components or scroll helpers. Leaf props
use their existing data fields and flattened
`UiPlacement` fields: either `rect` or `anchor`/`size` with optional `pivot` and
`offset`. Do not supply `kind`; the constructor supplies it. Panels/images also
accept canonical `background_for`. Plain `UiNode` children, including custom
components and existing scroll helpers, continue to compose normally.

`slider` takes the same `id`, optional `text`, `action`, `style` and placement
fields as `button`. `combobox` adds optional `expanded`. These preserve the
existing declarative control contract: they emit named actions, without storing
numeric values, selecting options or automatically binding project state.
Read `api.input.wasPressed("ApplySettings")` in `update` for a once-per-press
action, `wasReleased` for release and `isDown` for held input. The edge queries
are read-only, so multiple readers see the same edge. There is no `onClick`,
`onChange`, DOM event or hidden slider-value callback. Sustained slider state and
selection rules stay in project Luau; use the existing pointer/action APIs.

`screen` takes `id`, `node`, a dense `children` array and optional `budget`.
It copies ordinary author data and returns a screen; it does not publish it.
Call `api.ui.setRoot(screen)` normally.

`component` takes `id`, `component`, placement, optional dense `children`, and
optional `surface`. A surface is either `{kind="panel",style=...}` or
`{kind="image",asset=...,fit=...,slice=...,alt=...,style=...}`. It takes the
component's unchanged placement, receives the ID `componentId.."/surface"`, and
appears before the supplied children with `background_for={component=componentId}`.
That generated ID is reserved within the tree. The helper does not move children,
make coordinates relative, inherit styles, clip, reorder supplied children or
choose responsive arrangements. A scroll boundary still starts a separate
coordinate space.

`composeStyle(base?,override?)` copies its inputs; override fields win. Padding
merges by edge. Colors and all other values replace atomically. With no arguments
it returns `{}`. Constructors omit `style` when neither theme nor props specifies
one, preserving legacy unstyled text fitting; supplying `{}` opts into the
existing styled defaults. Ordinary authored data is copied, including theme,
rectangles, padding, color arrays, image slices and children. Registered nodes
returned by the kit's or module's `virtualList` and `virtualGrid` retain their identity:
the engine scroll helper owns their viewport, materialized children and scroll
state, and updates that same node when the host requests another visible range.
Pass those live nodes through as children; do not manually mutate or clone them.
This exception applies only to the exact registered helper node, not a plain
authored table with the same kind or ID.

The scroll constructors forward to the existing engine helpers, preserving the
original options, functions, registration and materialization lifecycle. They do
not clone `items`, `key` or `renderItem` callbacks. `viewport` uses explicit
`left`, `top`, `width`, `height`; content rectangles are local top-left/y-down.
Ordinary component children keep stage y-up coordinates: components do not
establish a relative coordinate space. The old `api.ui.scrollView`,
`api.ui.virtualList` and `api.ui.virtualGrid` remain compatibility paths. Prefer
the package entry points for new project UI.

`id(instanceId,role)` returns the instance ID plus `/` plus the role, escaping `%`
as `%25` and `/` as `%2F` in the role. It uses no counter or array index. Supply
stable instance IDs and stable semantic roles; list item identity remains the
project's responsibility.

Unknown constructor/theme/style fields and sparse children fail explicitly.
Unsupported callback, nested `placement` and automatic `layout` props include
actionable guidance toward the canonical action/placement contracts.
Copying rejects cycles, unsupported values, nesting above 64 levels and work
above 131072 visited values. These are bounded authoring checks; `api.ui.setRoot`
remains authoritative for numeric values, required fields, placement, IDs,
background scope, budgets and supported leaf styles. Strict layout diagnostics
still report foreground collisions. Publish the result through the normal
official player and verify its rendered text and input on the intended target.

# Official shared UI package

`@unone/ui` is the official, versioned pure Luau component package bundled with
Unone Core and the portable SDK. It constructs the existing typed UI tree for
`api.ui.setRoot`; the official Web/native players render that tree. Start here
for shared components, button components, card components and theme styles.
The project owns themes, content, state, action meanings and geometry.

## Discover and declare

```powershell
game api search "UI package"
game api search "shared components"
game api search "button component"
game api search "card component"
game api search "官方UI套件"
game api search "共用元件"
game api search "主題樣式"
game api search "create button"
game api search "slider component"
game api search "下拉選單"
game api search "virtual list"
game api search "button click"
game api search "按下瞬間"
game api describe ui.components.info
game api describe ui.components.create
game api describe ui.components.button
game api describe input.wasPressed
game api typings
```

CLI and MCP discovery share the same index. These searches lead to actual
`ui.components.create` / `ui.components.info` entrypoints. Control queries lead
directly to callable `ui.components.button`, `slider`, `combobox`, `scrollView`,
`virtualList` or `virtualGrid` descriptors. `"button click"`, `"button pressed"`,
`"按鈕點擊"`, `"按钮点击"`, `"按一下"` and `"按下瞬間"` lead to
`input.wasPressed`; `"release"` / `"放開"` lead to `input.wasReleased`, while
`"hold"` / `"長按"` lead to `input.isDown`. `"UI types"` / `"UI 型別"`
discover the canonical type route, and `"component relative coordinates"`
explains the unchanged-coordinate contract. `"font size"`,
`"text alignment"` and `"border padding"` still lead to `ui.setRoot` and the
[style contract](ui-styling.md); `"card background"` and `"component overlap"`
explain the canonical background scope checks.

Declare the exact bundled version in `project.unone.json`:

```json
{
  "runtime_packages": {
    "@unone/ui": "0.2.0"
  }
}
```

This is a project configuration fragment; keep the project's other fields.
`api.ui.components.info()` returns `UiComponentsInfo`: the bundled manifest
metadata (`name`, `version`, `kind`, `entry`, `api`, `license`) plus `declared`.
This works before a project declares the package. The package name is `@unone/ui`
and its current version is `0.2.0`. Calling other package helpers without declaring the
package reports `UI_PACKAGE_NOT_DECLARED` with the required fix. Unknown package
names, unsupported versions and disabled declarations fail explicitly at load.
Use the version shipped with the selected Core/SDK; there is no npm installation,
`require` import, filesystem module loader or dynamic package download.

The SDK includes the package source, documentation and canonical Luau types in
its verified inventory. An older runtime without this package cannot satisfy
the declaration; SDK preflight rejects that mismatch. A passing authoring
`verify` / `prepare` alone does not prove the selected exported runtime supports
the package or that a player rendered the result. Refresh the SDK, regenerate
`game api typings`, prepare/export and inspect the official target player.
New `project init` entries already inline the current canonical type contract.

## Keep the official types when upgrading

Use `EngineApi` for `Game.start`/`Game.update`, `UiApi` for the publication API,
`UiComponentKit` for a created kit, and `UiNode`, `UiScreen`, `UiStyle` and the
per-constructor props for authored data. These are the canonical types returned
by `game api typings`; do not maintain a second handwritten `EngineApi` or use
`ui:any` to bypass mismatches. For example:

```luau
function Game.update(api: EngineApi, dt: number)
    local ui: UiComponentKit = api.ui.components.create()
    local action: UiButtonNode = ui.button({id="apply",text="Apply",
        action="ApplySettings",rect={x=60,y=10,width=30,height=8}})
    api.ui.setRoot(ui.screen({id="settings",node="settings",children={action}}))
end
```

New project entry scripts contain an explicitly marked canonical block. After
upgrading the SDK, safely refresh that block while preserving the surrounding
game code:

```powershell
game --project <game-root> api typings --update-script gameplay.luau
```

This command requires exactly one own-line `-- BEGIN UNONE API TYPES` /
`-- END UNONE API TYPES` pair. It rejects missing, duplicate or malformed
markers without writing. For an older unmarked script, obtain the contract
with `game api typings`, review its initial integration and add the marker pair
around only that canonical block. `--output <file>` writes a complete type
contract file; never point it at an existing game entry script. It cannot be
combined with `--update-script`. Run strict Luau analysis and the project's
normal verify/prepare gates after refreshing. A compositor must preserve these
types when it inlines game fragments.

## Construct typed leaves and components

```luau
local ui: UiComponentKit = api.ui.components.create({
    text={font_size=2.4,text_align="start",color={0.9,0.95,1,1}},
    button={font_size=2,background={0.08,0.2,0.3,1},border_radius=0.6},
    panel={background={0.025,0.045,0.07,1},border_color={0.2,0.4,0.6,1},
        border_width=0.1,border_radius=1},
})

local function actionCard(id: string, x: number, title: string, action: string): UiComponentNode
    return ui.component({
        id=id,component="game.action_card",rect={x=x,y=30,width=35,height=45},
        surface={kind="panel"},
        children={
            ui.text({id=ui.id(id,"title"),text=title,
                rect={x=x+2,y=60,width=31,height=8}}),
            ui.button({id=ui.id(id,"action"),text="Open",action=action,
                rect={x=x+2,y=35,width=31,height=8}}),
        },
    })
end

api.ui.setRoot(ui.screen({id="menu",node="menu",children={
    actionCard("menu/inventory",10,"Inventory","OpenInventory"),
    actionCard("menu/settings",55,"Settings","OpenSettings"),
}}))
```

The numbers and action names above are project choices. The package supplies no
default palette, fonts, layout, responsive policy, manager or business behavior.
A custom Luau factory such as `actionCard` composes the official kit; existing
factories that return canonical nodes directly remain valid.

`create(theme?)` returns a `UiComponentKit` with these methods:

| Kit method | Result and input contract |
| --- | --- |
| `ui.text(props)` | `UiTextNode`; canonical text fields including `id`, `text`, placement and optional `style`. |
| `ui.button(props)` | `UiButtonNode`; canonical button fields including `id`, `text`, `action`, placement and optional `style`. |
| `ui.slider(props)` | `UiSliderNode`; `id`, optional `text`, semantic `action`, placement and optional `style`. The project owns the numeric value and drag mapping. |
| `ui.combobox(props)` | `UiComboBoxNode`; `id`, optional `text`, semantic `action`, optional `expanded`, placement and optional `style`. The project authors the option list and selected value. |
| `ui.panel(props)` | `UiPanelNode`; canonical decorative panel fields, placement, optional box style and `background_for`. |
| `ui.image(props)` | `UiImageNode`; canonical image fields including `asset`, placement, optional `fit`/`slice`/`alt`, box style and `background_for`. |
| `ui.component(props)` | `UiComponentNode`; `id`, `component`, placement, optional `children` and `surface`. |
| `ui.screen(props)` | `UiScreen`; `id`, `node`, `children` and optional `budget`. A root has no placement or style; call `api.ui.setRoot(root)` explicitly. |
| `ui.scrollView(options)` | `UiNode`; delegates to the existing finite-content helper with unchanged `UiScrollOptions`. |
| `ui.virtualList(options)` | `UiNode`; delegates to the existing registered virtual-list helper with unchanged `UiVirtualOptions`. |
| `ui.virtualGrid(options)` | `UiNode`; delegates to the existing registered virtual-grid helper with unchanged `UiVirtualGridOptions`. |
| `ui.id(instanceId,role)` | Stable `instanceId.."/"..escapedRole` string; role escapes `%` as `%25` and `/` as `%2F`. Both inputs must be non-empty. Also available as `api.ui.components.id`. |
| `ui.composeStyle(base?,override?)` | A fresh `UiStyle`; also available as `api.ui.components.composeStyle`. |

Every constructor above also exists directly on `api.ui.components`, with the
same props and no theme defaults: `api.ui.components.button({...})` is valid.
Use a created kit when sharing a theme, or module constructors when no theme is
needed. `api.ui.component` does not exist. Props omit `kind`; each constructor chooses its
canonical kind. Placement is **flattened**: pass `rect={...}` or both
`anchor="top_right",size={...}` directly on props, exactly as in `UiPlacement`.
A nested `placement` table, missing placement, or both forms is invalid for a
leaf/component. `screen` instead uses root props, and scroll wrappers retain
their `viewport` options. All canonical leaf fields remain available; virtual
wrappers retain the existing engine-managed scroll registry and add no gameplay
state or manager.

Components do not transform child coordinates. A component at `x=40` with a
child at `x=5` still places that child at stage `x=5`, outside the component; it
does not place it at `x=45`. In stage space children keep 0..100 coordinates with
y pointing up. Scroll content instead uses local top-left coordinates with y
pointing down; its viewport belongs to the containing coordinate space. Follow
[the scroll contract](ui-scroll.md) rather than adding a component-relative
transform. Child order is retained. Use `api.ui.getViewport()` in the
project's View to choose a responsive composition and explicit dimensions.

## Read semantic actions

Buttons and comboboxes publish their `action` through the existing input system.
The same action can come from a mapped key or a headless test. Read it in
`Game.update` rather than passing an `onClick` function:

```luau
if api.input.wasPressed("ApplySettings") then
    applySettings() -- project-owned model change
end
if api.input.isDown("MoveRight") then
    moveRight(dt) -- project-owned continuous behavior
end
if api.input.wasReleased("Charge") then
    releaseCharge() -- project-owned release behavior
end
```

`wasPressed(action)` means down now and not down in the previous successful
tick; `wasReleased(action)` means up now and down previously. `isDown(action)`
means held now. All reads are non-consuming and stable within an update, so two
readers see the same edge. Only successful ticks advance the prior snapshot;
rendering, observations and virtual-scroll requests do not. Initially actions
are released, and omitted actions are released on the next input snapshot.
These are snapshot transitions, not a queued OS-event stream: an entire pulse
between snapshots is not buffered. Keep action meanings, selected options,
slider values and screen transitions in project Luau. The kit does not install
callbacks or automatically modify a model.

The slider leaf supplies an authored interaction surface and semantic action;
it has no `value`, `min`, `max` or `onChange` prop. Map the normalized UI pointer
through the project's explicit rect to choose a value. A combobox's `expanded`
flag is authored state; the engine does not invent options or a selection model.
The constructors retain their canonical control contracts rather than adding
project-specific widget behavior.

### Scroll wrappers

Both the module and themed kit expose the same existing helpers. For example,
`ui.scrollView({id="help",viewport={left=10,top=10,width=80,height=80},content={}})`
uses the same options as `api.ui.scrollView`. The legacy `api.ui.scrollView`,
`virtualList` and `virtualGrid` entrypoints remain compatible. Container wrappers
have no theme `style`; virtual `renderItem` callbacks remain UI-pure, use stable
keys and return local nodes. Scrolling does not run `Game.update`. Current
native/legacy DOM hosts reject scrolling explicitly; package wrappers do not
expand host support.

## Theme copying and surfaces

`theme: UiComponentsTheme` accepts only optional `text`, `button`, `panel`, `image`,
`slider` and `combobox` `UiStyle`
defaults. There is no component-level style inheritance. Each leaf copies its
kind's defaults and then its explicit style; explicit fields win. Padding merges
by edge, while RGBA arrays replace as a whole. Neither style input, the theme,
props nor an earlier result is mutated. An omitted theme/style leaves `style`
omitted and retains canonical legacy fitting; an explicit empty style selects
[explicit typography defaults](ui-styling.md#coordinates-and-defaults).

Ordinary authored tables are copied. Nodes returned by the official
`virtualList` and `virtualGrid` helpers are engine-managed live handles: the
composer preserves their exact registered identity so later viewport requests
update the published tree. Do not clone or manually mutate those handles. The
exception is recognized by the engine's private registry, not by a node name or
an ID pattern; ordinary hand-authored nodes remain independent copies. Existing
[scroll lifecycle and purity rules](ui-scroll.md) continue to apply.

```luau
local base: UiStyle = {padding={left=1,right=1},color={1,1,1,1}}
local variant = ui.composeStyle(base,{padding={right=2},color={1,0.8,0.2,1}})
-- variant padding is left=1,right=2; base and both RGBA arrays remain independent.
```

A component's optional `surface` chooses `kind="panel"` or `kind="image"` and
accepts that kind's canonical `style`, `asset`, `fit`, `slice` and `alt` fields as
applicable. Image surfaces require an asset. The helper prepends one background
leaf with ID `id.."/surface"`, copies the component's explicit placement unchanged,
and adds `background_for={component=id}`. The remaining children keep their
coordinates and order. Reserve that generated ID when choosing child roles.
Omitting `surface` adds no background node.

The surface is ordinary canonical data. `setRoot` checks its ancestor, coordinate
space and bounds; strict preview exempts only later fully contained descendants.
Foreground collisions, partial coverage, unrelated siblings and later occlusion
still fail inspection. See [explicit background scopes](ui-styling.md#explicit-background-scopes).
The helper does not move, resize, clip, auto-layout or weaken overlap checks.
Canonical styles, bounds, image slicing and node budgets remain authoritative.

## Verify the actual player and fonts

Keep `renderer_mode: "official"` and inspect the exported player, including
readable type, overlap and real input at the target viewport sizes. See
[font packaging and coverage](ui-styling.md#package-a-font-catalog). A loaded
font face does not prove coverage for CJK, punctuation or arrows. The existing
`scripts/verify-ui-example-browser.mjs` observer can record real Web input,
screenshots, Canvas text and semantic snapshots; its local-export path runs
`scripts/audit-ui-fonts.py` against packaged font cmap tables. A project's plan
can require packaged glyph coverage. Inspect the screenshots as well as reports.

A pasted `<body data-player-...>` block is a host diagnostic HTML snapshot. It
can identify the official renderer and expose timings, but Canvas pixels are
not included in that text and the renderer marker does not prove a particular
UI package version. Use a screenshot to assess appearance, the read-only runtime
snapshot for the published tree/actions, and `ui.components.info()` for package
metadata. Do not replace the renderer or reconstruct the UI with DOM to make
these diagnostics readable.

# ScrollView and virtual collections (Web)

Use `api.ui.scrollView` for small, irregular authored content. Use
`api.ui.virtualList` for long fixed-height rows, or `api.ui.virtualGrid` for
fixed-size cells. All three return a real `scroll_view` node; put that node
in the `children` of the screen passed to `api.ui.setRoot`.

## The coordinate rule

- `viewport={left,top,width,height}` is top-left/y-down in the containing space.
  At the screen level it is relative to the stage, not the browser window.
  Do not pass old stage `rect={x,y,...}` to a helper's viewport. The engine
  performs the y-up transport conversion; callers do not.
- Every content rect, including component children, is **local top-left/y-down**:
  `{x=0,y=0}` is the viewport's top-left before scrolling. x uses percent of stage
  width; y uses percent of stage height, not percent of the scroll viewport.
- Nested scroll viewports are local to the parent's content. Their children
  start a new local space. Anchors are rejected inside scroll content.
- All content x/y must be non-negative. Negative-origin content is rejected;
  author content from y=0 and let the controller move it upward. This is not
  an infinite pan/zoom surface.
- Ordinary ScrollView never arranges your content. Its extent is measured from
  the supplied rectangles. Do not set contentHeight, maxScroll or itemCount.

```lua
local help = api.ui.scrollView({
 id="help", viewport={left=10,top=15,width=80,height=70},
 content={
  {kind="text",id="intro",text="Introduction",rect={x=0,y=0,width=80,height=10}},
  {kind="text",id="more",text="More",rect={x=0,y=100,width=80,height=10}},
 },
})
api.ui.setRoot({kind="screen",id="settings",node="help",children={help}})
```

## VirtualList

`renderItem(item,index,key)` returns a **non-empty array** of UI nodes with
cell-local rects. It does not include the row/column position. It must be a
pure view function: no gameplay mutation, randomness, input, saves or jobs.
It may run on a host UI request while simulation is paused.

`index` is one-based. The key function is also UI-pure and may be called on
every republish; keys are validated before materializing nodes. Sizes are
finite positive numbers; gaps finite non-negative numbers; columns are integer
1..1024. Unknown helper options are errors, not silently ignored.

```lua
local list = api.ui.virtualList({
 id="inventory", viewport={left=10,top=15,width=80,height=70},
 items=items, key="id", rowHeight=8, gapY=1,
 renderItem=function(item,index,key)
  return {{kind="button",id="item_"..key,text=item.name,action="Inspect_"..key,
   rect={x=0,y=0,width=80,height=8}}}
 end,
})
api.ui.setRoot({kind="screen",id="inventory_screen",node="inventory",children={list}})
```

`items` is an array; `key` is a string field name or a function returning a
unique non-empty string. Keys describe the item, **not its array position**.
IDs of returned nodes must also be globally unique and stable across filtering.
Empty arrays are supported. Maximum 100,000 keys; normal node budgets still
apply to the materialized window. Lua items and callbacks are never serialized.

## VirtualGrid

Same options as VirtualList plus required `columns`, `columnWidth`, and optional
`gapX`. `rowHeight` means the cell's height, **not including gapY**. Columns are
an explicit author decision and must fit the viewport. No implicit reflow.

```lua
local grid = api.ui.virtualGrid({
 id="skills", viewport={left=10,top=15,width=80,height=70},
 items=skills, key="id", columns=8, columnWidth=9, gapX=1,
 rowHeight=16, gapY=1,
 renderItem=function(item,index,key)
  return {{kind="button",id="skill_"..key,text=item.name,action="Inspect_"..key,
   rect={x=0,y=0,width=9,height=16}}}
 end,
})
api.ui.setRoot({kind="screen",id="skill_screen",node="skills",children={grid}})
```

## Shared optional settings and lifecycle

- `enabled=false`: retain offset but disable scroll input and content actions;
  use while a foreground modal blocks the collection.
- `resetKey="filter-name"`: change to explicitly return to the beginning.
  Otherwise, the same node ID retains its position: unchanged data retains the
  numeric offset; edits retain the first visible key where possible, then clamp.
- `wheelRect={left,top,width,height}`: optional wider stage rectangle receiving wheel input, e.g. a
  panel's blank area. Nested ScrollViews use their viewport only.
- Ordinary ScrollView additionally accepts `axis="vertical"` (default),
  `"horizontal"` or `"both"`. Virtual collections are vertical only.
- Removal disposes the host controller and Lua data-source registration.
  Async requests carry a revision; removed/filtered stale requests are ignored.
- Render, pointer hit regions and keyboard reveal share one clipped projection.

## Web host integration

Use `createUiScrollHost` from `web/shared/ui-scroll.mjs` once per stage. Pass
`canvas`, `stage`, `onAction`, and `requestWindow(request)`; the latter sends
`backend.request({kind:"ui",request})`, accepts the returned snapshot and redraws.
Run `scroll.draw(snapshot)` before Canvas/UI motion/accessibility projection.
Route touch through `scroll.pointer(event,kind,hit)` before ordinary UI input;
Route pointercancel/lostpointercapture through `scroll.pointer(event,"cancel")`;
use `scroll.cancel()` for a whole-surface pause/blur and `dispose()` on removal.
Normal pointer capture release must not clear the last keyboard scroll owner.
Do not send a simulation tick to materialize rows.

Default semantic controls identify themselves with `data-ui-control="node-id"`.
Hosts using another control projection pass `getFocusedNode(): nodeId?` and
`focusNode(nodeId): boolean` (true if focus succeeded). The controller has no
game-specific selector or node-name convention. Focus restoration is deferred
until after the host synchronizes its current controls.

The controller offers `scrollToKey(viewId,key)`, `ensureVisible(nodeId)`,
`navigate(nodeId,code)` and `report()`. Host semantic controls should call
ensureVisible on focus and use navigate for arrow/Home/End collection navigation.
Only materialized controls exist: do not expose 100,000 hidden DOM buttons.
When the host reorders/recreates semantic controls, suppress automatic old-focus
restoration while `scroll.isNavigating()` is true; otherwise it can scroll back
to the previous row before the requested target is materialized. Sliders,
comboboxes and editable fields retain their own keyboard input. Nested wheel
input chains to an outer view when the inner view reaches its edge, and nested
rails are clipped to ancestor viewports. This release uses direct touch dragging,
not momentum, elastic overscroll or variable-height measurement.

## Images, actions and foreground dialogs

An image is visual-only; a sibling button owns the action. Assets are stable
IDs declared in the project's asset manifest, not file paths or remote URLs:

```lua
renderItem=function(item,index,key)
 return {
  {kind="image",id="icon_"..key,asset=item.asset,fit="contain",
   rect={x=0,y=0,width=9,height=16}},
  {kind="button",id="hit_"..key,text="",action="Inspect_"..key,
   rect={x=0,y=0,width=9,height=16}},
 }
end
```

Buttons use the existing action input protocol: host `onAction(action)` queues
that action using `createHostInput().queueAction(action)`. In `Game.update`,
read `api.input.isDown(action)`; game-owned edge detection prevents repeated
activation when held. There is no new Lua `onAction` hook:

```lua
local wasOpen=false
function Game.update(api,dt)
 local down=api.input.isDown("Inspect_known_item")
 if down and not wasOpen then selectedId="known_item" end
 wasOpen=down
 publish(api) -- Rebuild the view from game state; renderItem only reads it.
end
```

Keep a modal-blocked collection in the root with `enabled=false`, and keep its
node ID/resetKey unchanged. Disabling only affects this collection, not the
simulation or other UI. Publish foreground dialog nodes **after** the collection:
array order is paint order. Reuse your project's dialog/overlay and focus trap;
this API does not invent a modal node or a second game flow. Close the dialog,
republish with enabled=true, then restore focus to the same stable item key.
For key-preserving edits above the viewport, the Web controller retains the
first visible key when it still exists; deleting that key falls back to clamped
offset. Filtering `items` alone follows that edit-preservation rule. To reset
on filtering, explicitly change resetKey.
None of the three minimal examples automatically changes a filter: the caller
owns its filter state and resetKey.

Screen `id` is its stable identity; `node` is an inspectable game-defined route
label, not a reference to a child. Both are required non-empty strings.

Canvas hosts without a controller project offset zero. The legacy DOM and
native hosts currently report `UI_HOST_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`; native input,
screen-reader certification and variable-height virtualization are not claimed.

- `node --test web/shared/ui-scroll.test.mjs web/shared/ui-scroll-host.test.mjs web/shared/canvas-ui.test.mjs web/shared/runtime-core.test.mjs`
  checks shared projection, controller lifecycle, 100,000-key bounds and UI-only transport.
- `cargo test -p unone-engine virtual_ui_materializes_without_a_game_tick`
  checks actual Lua 10,000-item window requests, stale/invalid ranges and unchanged simulation/RNG.
- `cargo test -p unone-engine scroll_helpers_cover_empty_data_nested_views_and_fail_loudly`
  checks empty data, nested content and invalid helper configuration.
- `tests/scroll-parity-project` covers initial, modal-disabled, filtered and empty
  states through the official CLI/Web export parity gate. The parity fixture has
  10,000 Lua items; the 100,000-key controller test is not an end-to-end performance claim.

# Game authoring contract

Use Unone's official player and renderer by default. Keep gameplay in Luau and use engine APIs for presentation. Do not obtain a WebGL/OpenGL context or write a separate browser host for an ordinary game.

Before adding effects, run `game api search particle`, `game api describe particle.play`, `game api search shader`, and `game systems list --json`. Author scene `particle_effects` for explosions, thrusters, sparks, smoke, trails and auras. Keep the particle system enabled when using these effects. Custom shaders go through scene `shader_materials` and `api.shader.*`; the engine owns GPU compilation and rendering. Use presentation Bloom when appropriate.

`player.presentation.json` selects `renderer_mode: official`. Replace the renderer only as an explicitly selected extension for a stated project requirement, never merely to add effects or shaders: select `renderer_mode: custom`, set `renderer_module`, and list the entry plus local dependencies in `renderer_files`. This trusted Web extension is not a sandbox and does not claim official renderer coverage. Report the selected mode in validation.

Run verify for the scaffold, then `game project preflight --target web` and `game project prepare --target web --output <new-output-directory>` to obtain an official player export and launch descriptor. Inspect SDK availability if preflight reports a missing runtime. The starter tests only check onboarding and movement; add game-specific acceptance and inspect rendered output before delivery.
